Before answering the route and the two decisions, the author asked whether the model wants to distinguish a raw vault from a business vault.
verbatim: Before I answer the questions, do you want to make a distinction between a raw vault and a business vault?

summary: Proposed yes: raw vault holds what the source delivered (insert-only, generated from key declarations, source-computed columns kept as delivered, only loss-free technical conversions); business vault holds every interpretation (derived values, the calculation register, inferred links such as payment-to-invoice matching, role readings, PIT and bridge structures), rebuilt from the raw vault, as 140 and ADR-0015 already imply. Named grey zones for the author and how the split sharpens decisions 1 and 2; unreviewed, not yet an ADR.

The author asked whether the raw vault is per source: with several administrations covering the same business entities (an acquisition, several or legacy core banking systems), a raw vault per source, one shared raw vault, or integration in the business vault.
verbatim: Okay, and the raw vault would be by source, right? This is what I'm interested in, if we have e.g. done an acquisition of another company, with its own administration and corresponding quirks, do we set up a new structure for it, or does it all go into the entities that were set up for the initial source? So my question is, if we have administrations/databases that cover in essence the same business entities (multiple core banking systems, legacy core banking systems), do we set up a raw vault for each of them, or do we all cram them into the same raw vault, or is this something we handle at the business vault layer?

summary: Proposed one raw vault, split by source where descriptions live and shared where identity lives: hubs per business concept, shared across sources only when the key is the same identifier with the same meaning (e.g. IBAN); otherwise keys qualified by a key-space (collision) code; satellites always per source; links shared only for the same declared relationship. Matching across key spaces is interpretation and goes to the business vault as same-as links with evidence and confidence, except mappings a source itself delivers (a migration's old-to-new table), which load as raw. For WWI: name satellites per source and carry a key-space code from the first load. From general knowledge, unreviewed.
The author asked what the raw vault is for and what the business vault is for.
verbatim: can you tell me what the raw vault is for and what the business vault is for?

summary: Stated the purpose of each layer: raw vault as memory (all data, all history, insert-only, integration only on certain keys, audit and lineage, rebuild base, signal of source change; generated, judgement only in keys); business vault as understanding (values the source does not store, rules and calculations defined once, uncertain integration such as same-as links, role readings and payment matching, time views, helper structures; rebuildable, adjudicated, each object citing its decision); marts thin. Logged after the reply because the desktop workspace was starting.

The author proposed calculation engines for every business rule and calculation beyond basic arithmetic: software (Python, numpy, pandas) with versioning, unit tests and inline documentation, each result stored with the engine version, treated as a separate source; asked where they belong.
verbatim: it should be connected right now. Where do you place calculation engines? For any application of business rules and calculations (except for very basic addition and multiplication) I envisage to have calculation engines, which are more like software (think python programs) then doing it in SQL. The thing with calculation engines, is that they should have versioning, unit testing, inline documentation etc. I imagine building them with e.g. numpy and panda. If a calculation is performed, ideally it would store the value and the version of the calculation engine. I see this as a separate source. What do you thinkg? PS the workspace should be up now.

summary: Agreed and placed engines as deterministic machinery outside both vaults, an internal source whose results load insert-only under their own source code; conditions proposed: version means code plus locked dependencies, each result row carries engine, version, run and the as-of of its inputs, versions side by side so a release's impact is the diff of two versions on the same inputs, money never in float, a fixed pipeline order without cycles, the source's computed columns as test oracles; revises the earlier raw-vault test to 'did a system say this'. Put three choices to the author: the SQL-versus-engine boundary, recalculation policy on a new version, and how far back. Unreviewed.

The author ruled on the three engine choices (boundary agreed; recompute everything when compute and storage allow, a new version is new data even with equal values; corrected inputs rerun, using bitemporality), asked for everything to be stored in the repository, and asked whether marts derive from the raw and business vault, proposing a dimensional model per distinct use case.

13. Agree
14. I think the uncomfortable answer is: it depends. If we have enough compute (and storage), I'd recompute everything, and using a bitemporal database structure, we can time travel. If the version changes, this means the data changes, even if the outcome is the same.

3: engine results go in the raw vault. Open fall back: if there is not enough compute, first let's try it from a cut-off date. If still not enough, only do going forward. It always requires human adjudication.
12: Like you said, dimensions should be shared. So we're focused mainly on fact tables. I think there is a consideration / deliberation necessary if for a new question a fact table only kind of fits. We should do an analysis then, to see how much we have to alter the fact table to make it compatible with the new request and how much we are drifting away from the original intent. If we can formalize these questions, then fine, otherwise human adjudication is necessary. Under normal circumstances this is not a continuous process / going concern thing. Expanding fact tables to fit new business questions is quite the fundamental decision. If you can list a number of considerations to base the decision on, that is very helpful. Maybe when enough experience has been built up the decision making can be automated.
